[F1 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
C2: The platform itself never recorded the driver arriving: driver_arrived_at is null (F4). The only arrival indication is the driver's own tap, made 600 m from the pickup (F5), so condition (ii) of NS-1 fails and the $6.61 no-show fee cannot stand. [F4 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: The waiting requirement also fails: the driver was stationary 12:05:55–12:09:25 at a point 600 m from the pickup (F2), i.e. not at the pickup point, so his 3 min 30 s of waiting was not waiting at the pick-up location within 200 m as NS-1(iii) requires. [F2 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]

[F12 F1 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]

(F9) while the driver's message (F8) and his cancellation message (F10) place him only on his own assertion of being "here". [F8 F9 F10] [NS-1 NS-2]

C7: The driver has 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F17), so this recurring pattern supports (but does not by itself decide) the account-review request attached to the refund. [F17] [NS-2]

claims.assertion: The system records show the driver did press "I'm Here" for this trip (F5, tap at 12:06:15), so the cancellation was processed as a rider no-show under the arrival-button process rather than as an unexplained driver cancellation.

The driver's own records show a genuine wait at a fixed spot: he was stationary for 3 min 30 s from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 (F2), and his written account states he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes before cancelling (F12).

The rider was told the car was waiting and where: chat #1 at 12:06 says "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out", and the rider answered at 12:07 that she was at the pickup point (F8, F9), so both sides were actively engaged while the driver held his position until he cancelled at 12:09:25 (F3, F10).
The chat record for this trip is complete — three messages, every one timestamped (F11) — so nothing in the exchange was lost, and the driver's account does not contradict any recorded message.

External conditions give no reason to doubt the driver's account: the only traffic reading was Jalan Besar at band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents near the route (F13, F14) and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F15); the fee itself was the standard, un-surged cancellation amount (F6, F7).

If the panel is not satisfied that the arrival and continuous-wait requirements are met, the correct outcome under the policy is the full return of the $6.61 cancellation fee (F6) with no account action against the driver, since the complaint's factual premise is that the driver was never at the pickup point (F1, F4).

The driver is a long-standing, high-volume account (2,295 days, 4.67 rating, 464 trips in 90 days) with a single upheld no-show in 90 days (F17); that history supports keeping the case at the ordinary fee level and does not itself establish wrongdoing in this case.

weaknesses: The GPS record directly undercuts the driver on NS-1 (ii): his closest approach to the pickup point was 599 m (F1) and he never came within 200 m, while he tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 from 600 m away (F5).

NS-1 (iii) also fails on the record: the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all — driver_arrived_at is null (F4) — and he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap (F5), so no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup can be shown from the system data.

Because (ii) and (iii) fail, NS-2 points the other way and even contemplates an account flag for tapping "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius (F5); the rider's account (F9) and the 12:09 cancellation message (F10) fit that reading, and the driver's contrary account is only a statement (F12), which loses to the system records.
Profile facts cannot cure this: the driver's one prior upheld no-show in 90 days (F17) may be read as a pattern rather than as good character if the panel finds the arrival tap was misuse.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 599 m and he was never within 200 m of Bugis Junction (F1). He therefore was not at the pick-up location according to GPS data when he tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15, which was 600 m away, and he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap (F5).

The platform itself never recorded the driver arriving: driver_arrived_at is null (F4). The only arrival indication is the driver's own tap, made 600 m from the pickup (F5), so condition (ii) of NS-1 fails and the $6.61 no-show fee cannot stand.

The waiting requirement also fails: the driver was stationary 12:05:55–12:09:25 at a point 600 m from the pickup (F2), i.e. not at the pickup point, so his 3 min 30 s of waiting was not waiting at the pick-up location within 200 m as NS-1(iii) requires.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" (F12) is contradicted by the GPS record that his closest approach was 599 m (F1) and by the null arrival record (F4); under the system-record rule the GPS and timeline facts prevail, so the statement cannot establish NS-1.

The chat confirms the rider was at the pickup point and saw no car: the rider wrote at 12:07 "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" (F9) while the driver's message (F8) and his cancellation message (F10) place him only on his own assertion of being "here".

Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him > 200 m from the pickup (600 m, F5), the case also warrants flagging the driver's account for misuse of the arrival/cancellation button under Ryde's fraud list, alongside the full refund of the $6.61 fee charged (F6).
The driver has 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days (F17), so this recurring pattern supports (but does not by itself decide) the account-review request attached to the refund.

The $6.61 cancellation fee charged (F6) is a rider no-show fee only if NS-1 (i)-(iii) are all satisfied; none of them is satisfied here, so the full $6.61 must be refunded to the rider (as a Ryde voucher per NS-7).

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" and did wait ~3 min 30 s in one place (F2, F5), so on timing alone the waiting duration looks compatible with NS-1(iii); the case turns entirely on the 600 m distance, and the other side will argue the 200 m radius is only a data-layer parameter (空缺 G2) rather than a published Ryde rule.

The rider's own profile is unremarkable (4.4 rating, 0 disputes, F16) and the driver's is long-standing with 464 trips (F17); the driver may argue he was delayed by traffic on Jalan Besar, band 3, 20–29 km/h (F13), even though that is not congestion severe enough to be a defence and no incident is recorded (F14).

claims.assertion: The system records show the driver did press "I'm Here" for this trip (F5, tap at 12:06:15), so the cancellation was processed as a rider no-show under the arrival-button process rather than as an unexplained driver cancellation.

The driver's own records show a genuine wait at a fixed spot: he was stationary for 3 min 30 s from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 (F2), and his written account states he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than three minutes before cancelling (F12).

The rider was told the car was waiting and where: chat #1 at 12:06 says "I'm here already, silver Toyota Altis, please come out", and the rider answered at 12:07 that she was at the pickup point (F8, F9), so both sides were actively engaged while the driver held his position until he cancelled at 12:09:25 (F3, F10).
The chat record for this trip is complete — three messages, every one timestamped (F11) — so nothing in the exchange was lost, and the driver's account does not contradict any recorded message.

External conditions give no reason to doubt the driver's account: the only traffic reading was Jalan Besar at band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents near the route (F13, F14) and fair weather with 0.0 mm rain (F15); the fee itself was the standard, un-surged cancellation amount (F6, F7).

If the panel is not satisfied that the arrival and continuous-wait requirements are met, the correct outcome under the policy is the full return of the $6.61 cancellation fee (F6) with no account action against the driver, since the complaint's factual premise is that the driver was never at the pickup point (F1, F4).

The driver is a long-standing, high-volume account (2,295 days, 4.67 rating, 464 trips in 90 days) with a single upheld no-show in 90 days (F17); that history supports keeping the case at the ordinary fee level and does not itself establish wrongdoing in this case.

weaknesses: The GPS record directly undercuts the driver on NS-1 (ii): his closest approach to the pickup point was 599 m (F1) and he never came within 200 m, while he tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 from 600 m away (F5).

NS-1 (iii) also fails on the record: the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all — driver_arrived_at is null (F4) — and he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap (F5), so no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup can be shown from the system data.

Because (ii) and (iii) fail, NS-2 points the other way and even contemplates an account flag for tapping "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius (F5); the rider's account (F9) and the 12:09 cancellation message (F10) fit that reading, and the driver's contrary account is only a statement (F12), which loses to the system records.
Profile facts cannot cure this: the driver's one prior upheld no-show in 90 days (F17) may be read as a pattern rather than as good character if the panel finds the arrival tap was misuse.

points.response: A tap is only (i) of NS-1; the same record shows the tap was made 600 m from the pickup and the driver stayed within 200 m for 0 s afterwards (F5), so the tap does not make the cancellation a valid rider no-show under NS-1 — and NS-0 routes it to NS-1/NS-2, not to automatic validity.

The 3 min 30 s stationary period (F2) was spent 600 m from the pickup point, not at it, so it is not a wait "at the pick-up location" as NS-1(iii) requires; the written account (F12) is a statement contradicted by GPS (F1, F5) and by the null arrival record (F4), and system records win.

The exchange actually shows the opposite: the rider said at 12:07 "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" (F9) and the driver's only replies were an unsupported "I'm here already" (F8) and the 12:09 cancellation (F10) — engagement in chat does not put the car inside the 200 m arrival radius, where GPS shows it never was (F1, F5).

A complete chat record (F11) does not supply the missing GPS elements: even on a complete record, driver_arrived_at is null (F4) and the driver's arrival tap was 600 m out (F5), so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) remain unsatisfied.

Band 3 on Jalan Besar, 20–29 km/h, with no incidents and fair weather (F13, F14, F15) explains no failure to reach the pickup point while stationary at a fixed spot for 3 min 30 s (F2), and the standard un-surged fee (F6, F7) is simply the fee I ask to have refunded.

I accept the refund of the full $6.61 (F6); I do not drop the account-review request, because NS-2 expressly contemplates a flag when "I'm Here" is tapped outside the pickup radius, as it was here at 600 m (F5).

The driver's history (F17) is not offered as proof of wrongdoing but as the pattern ground for the NS-2 flag: one upheld no-show in 90 days plus a tap 600 m from the pickup (F5) is exactly the "repeated" signal NS-2 addresses.

The 599 m closest-approach figure (F1) is a GPS measurement of where the car ended up, not proof of what the driver knew or intended when he tapped; the tap itself is on record at 12:06:15 (F5), so NS-1(i) is satisfied on the record even if the radius requirement in NS-1(ii) is measured against a 200 m figure that Ryde has never published.

A null driver_arrived_at (F4) means the platform did not auto-confirm arrival; NS-1(i) expressly allows arrival by the driver's own tap, which is exactly what F5 records, so the absence of an automatic confirmation does not by itself defeat the case.

The driver was in one fixed place for 3 min 30 s (F2) and told the rider he was waiting and asked her to come out (F8); the record therefore shows a real, continuous wait by the driver of the length NS-1(iii) describes, and the only disputed element is the metre distance of the waiting spot.

The driver's statement (F12) is not contradicted on timing — F2 confirms the 3 min 30 s of waiting and F5 confirms the tap — so the only correction the system record makes is to the location word "pickup", not to the fact of waiting.

The rider's message (F9) says she saw no car, but it is her own unverified assertion; the opposing side itself relies on the driver's chat messages (F8, F10) as evidence of what happened, and those establish that the driver was holding a position and inviting her out until 12:09 (F10).

The account flag the opponent asks for is not automatic: NS-2 attaches it only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius (F5), and the radius itself is an unpublished data-layer parameter, so a flag is premature and should not be added as a matter of course.
A single prior upheld no-show in 90 days (F17) against a 2,295-day, 464-trip record (F17) is not a "recurring pattern", and profile facts may not be used to decide the case in any event.

I withdraw the suggestion that F2 and F12 together satisfy the "at the pickup point" element of NS-1: the GPS record places the waiting spot 600 m from the pickup (F2, F1) and the platform never recorded arrival (F4), so the honest reading is that the location element fails and only the fee question remains.

If the location element fails, NS-2 gives the rider the full return of the $6.61 fee (F6) by voucher (NS-7); my client does not resist the fee being returned, and his 6.3-year, 4.67-rating record (F17) supports the ordinary fee outcome rather than account action.
